items.text_snippet: Sealion Energy – Battery Performance Enhancement Skip to content Home Technology Markets About Home Technology Markets About Contact Home Technology Markets About Contact Home Technology Markets About Contact Contact BATTERY PERFORMANCE, REIMAGINED 10x Longer Life. Less Downtime. Lower Cost BATTERY PERFORMANCE, REIMAGINED 10x Longer Life. Less Downtime. Lower Cost Challenges We are Addressing CYCLE-LIFE 2X-10X extension SAFETY Prevent undesirable chemical reactions CHARGE TIME Accelerating electron and Li+ transport CHEMISTRY AGNOSTIC Compatible with solid-state and beyond lithium cells REGENERATION Regenerate cells at end of life Patented Process and Materials for Electrode Surface Engineering TECHNOLOGY A Material-level Approach To Battery Life Every battery that degrades faster than planned increases cost, reduces system uptime, and creates avoidable waste. SeaLion’s patented process applies ultra-thin nanocomposite coatings to battery electrodes to protect critical interfaces, preserve performance, and extend useful battery life by 10x – without changing the underlying chemistry. DEGRADATION • Particles crack or lose contact • Electrical pathways weaken • Capacity and efficiency fade. COATING • Ultra-thin conformal nanocomposite layer • Helps shield active surfaces • Targets interface stability during cycling REGENERATION • Focus on preserving material pathways • Supports longer useful life • Built around recovery and reliability MARKETS Where Battery Degradation Creates Real Business Pain Battery degradation is not an abstract technical problem. In every market SeaLion targets, it has a direct, measurable impact on performance, operational cost, revenue, and competitive position. Robotics and Autonomous systems As Industrial robots, AMRs, and autonomous platform deployments scale from tens to hundreds to thousands of units, battery management becomes a fleet cost and logistics problem. Improvement in cycle life with SeaLion’s battery is a significant operational savings to our customers. Grid and Commercial Energy Storage Grid-scale storage, commercial BESS, and high-cycle industrial systems project economics depend on the number of productive cycles a system can deliver. Degradation that reduces capacity by 20% in year three is effectively a write-down of project value. Every cycle of additional productive life with SeaLion’s battery, improves project IRR. Defence & Critical Systems Drone, UMVs, mobile tactical systems and other mission-critical platforms cannot tolerate unpredictable battery degradation. Performance under extreme conditions — temperature, rate, repeated deep discharge — is a qualification requirement, not a preference. SeaLion's battery technology improves performance at the margins where it matters most. EV & Transportation Battery health is becoming a financial instrument in the EV market — affecting resale value, insurance rates, and warranty liability. With SeaLion’s battery, OEMs and fleet operators that can demonstrate longer, healthier battery life hold a direct commercial advantage in residual value and total cost of ownership. ABOUT SEALION ENERGY BUILDING LONGER-LIFE BATTERIES FOR DEMANDING APPLICATIONS SeaLion Energy is a Carnegie Mellon spinout building longer-life batteries for robotics and advanced energy applications using patented technology that protects and regenerates critical battery materials. Our team combines world-class materials science with the commercial and engineering expertise needed to take technology to market. Founding Team We are hiring. items.title: Domestic, circular supply chain for EV batteries - College of Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University
items.text_snippet: Domestic, circular supply chain for EV batteries - College of Engineering at Carnegie Mellon University Skip to Main Content Carnegie Mellon College of Engineering Home Page Carnegie Mellon College of Engineering Home Page Menu Carnegie Mellon College of Engineering Home Page Carnegie Mellon College of Engineering Home Page Research Education Industry & Innovation About the College Student life News Events Student life Alumni engagement Contact For Faculty & Staff Directory Site Map Search Search Popular Searches Admitted students Master’s of AI Engineering Engineering Magazine graduate programs Manufacturing Futures Institute Rethink the Rink Social Media CMUEngineering College of Engineering CMUEngineering CMUEngineering RSS Feed @CMUEngineering Home News Domestic, circular supply chain for EV batteries by Kaitlyn Landram SeaLion Energy, a CMU-led startup, received funding from the U.S. Department of Energy ARPA-E to extend EV battery life and facilitate repair and reuse to reduce waste. The use of passenger electric vehicles (EVs) is expected to rise to 28% by 2030 and 58% by 2040, globally. The existing supply chain for EV batteries relies mostly on recycling to close the loop to recover critical minerals such as cobalt, nickel, or copper. However, conventional battery recycling methods are energy-intensive, produce significant quantities of greenhouse gases, and lead to large volumes of waste deposited in landfills. To catalyze the transition from a linear to a circular supply chain for domestic EV batteries, the U.S. Department of Energy Advanced Research Projects - Energy (ARPA-E) has announced $36 million for 13 projects to accelerate technologies and pursue solutions to extend battery life and facilitate repair and reuse to reduce waste. SeaLion Energy , a startup company founded by Reeja Jayan , professor of mechanical engineering and fellow of the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation , was selected to receive $1.6 million to develop a low-cost and low-greenhouse gas coating technology that significantly extends battery cycle life. SeaLion Energy’s project, known as TARDIS-J (Tunable Activation & Regeneration in Devices using In-Situ Jamming), will also reduce waste by regenerating “dead” battery cells. Redefining the future of energy storage, SeaLion Energy’s patented innovation also reduces charging times and improves operating safety. “We need to rethink the way batteries are manufactured from the ground up so that every element can be carefully designed, taking into consideration not just cost and performance but also what happens to the battery at end of life,” said Jayan. “When an EV driver wants to upgrade their vehicle, the battery should live on at a grid storage facility to power peoples’ homes; it shouldn’t sit in a landfill.” Each of the 13 ARPA-E funded projects will be managed under the Catalyzing Innovative Research for Circular Use of Long Lived Advanced Rechargeables (CIRCULAR) program. “ARPA-E turns bold ideas into transformative breakthroughs,” said ARPA-E Director Evelyn N. Wang. “We identified the need for more effective alternatives to the current battery recycling paradigm. I look forward to seeing how these CIRCULAR projects develop regeneration, repair, reuse, and remanufacture technologies to create a sustainable EV battery supply chain.” U.S. Congresswoman Summer Lee celebrated SeaLion’s achievement , “With projects like this, Pittsburgh is proving itself as a national leader in clean technology and sustainable innovation. Federal investments in transformative projects like SeaLion’s TARDIS-J are critical not only to supporting local talent and job creation but also to advancing a sustainable future. This is what it means to invest in our communities—solutions that benefit the people and the planet.” We need to focus on innovations that lead to cost-effective, scalable solutions that prolong battery life and reduce waste. Reeja Jayan , Professor , Mechanical Engineering With funding and comprehensive support from the Scott Institute for Energy Innovation, The Manufacturing Futures Institute , The Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship , and The Center for Technology Transfer and Enterprise Creation , Jayan credits CMU for helping to accelerate the spin-out of her startup company. “I am very grateful for this support,” she said. “I hope SeaLion Energy’s story can serve as a blueprint for the entrepreneurial pursuits of CMU students and faculty.” With climate change no longer just a possibility, but a reality, Jayan believes that everyone who is capable of doing something to mitigate it, should. “Instead of mining entire ecosystems out of existence to collect very limited minerals, we need to focus on innovations that lead to cost-effective, scalable solutions that prolong battery life and reduce waste. By doing so, we can realize a fully circular and domestic EV battery supply chain for the USA.” For media inquiries, please contact Kaitlyn Landram at klandram@andrew.cmu.edu . items.text_snippet: Smart Water Monitor – H2know by Conservation Labs Skip to content Search for: Overview Features How It Works Solutions About Us Buy Blog Help Homepage Mathias 2024-08-10T15:06:42-04:00 H 2 know TM Save water and money Meet H2know by Conservation Labs, an affordable smart water monitor to manage water consumption and protect you from water disasters. Features Peace of Mind Continuous monitoring of water use to identify leaks and email/text notifications for catastrophic leak events Leak events ranked by type with time of event, fixture classification, and amount of water used Sensor disconnect notifications Integrates with 3rd party shut-off device Save Water, Save Money Quickly determine what needs attention or action Current water use compared to weekly average for easy benchmarking All water events listed with duration and down to the fixture category Usage by date and daypart to see trends Ability to configure reports Easy and Flexible Easy to install, no cutting of pipes Adaptable to a property’s unique plumbing environment Configurable based on monitoring objectives How It Works New Way To Interpret Sound of Water Every time you do the dishes, flush the toilet, or use any water, the water rushes through the plumbing system to that location and creates a unique sound signature. You can hear it. H2know does too. H2know takes measurements from your pipe every second and uses our patented technology and machine learning approach to translate those signals to accurate water flow estimates, leak alerts, and water insights. This information is displayed on your H2know app so it is easy-to-read and to take action. View reports, find leaks, and discover ways to conserve water and save money! Connect to WiFi H2know uses WiFi to send usage data and alerts to your app. Attach to waterline No tools or plumber required, simply place H2know on the pipe and plug it into the nearest power outlet. Sign into the app Use the H2know app to set up and personalize your account. H2know immediately begins monitoring water usage. Residential Conservation Labs is pleased to make H2know available to residential homes in 2023. Apply to be one of the first to gain access and provide feedback on H2know. Learn More Commercial Real Estate Prevent high water bills and costly water damage with the easiest and most flexible to deploy smart water technology out there. H2know takes the guesswork out of water use monitoring, allowing you to take quick action with timely water insights and leak alerts. Learn More Restaurants A cost effective solution for restaurant operators to monitor commercial kitchen water consumption, detect leaks, and optimize conservation measures. Learn More Machines Introducing Sustainable Machines TM , an edge-to-cloud platform by Conservation Labs that provides high-resolution data on machine function and malfunction, helping OEMs and large service providers develop cost-effective condition monitoring and predictive maintenance programs. Learn More About Us Conservation Labs is an Amazon Alexa Fund portfolio company. We founded Conservation Labs to help you save money and better manage our natural resources. This is our big challenge: there are over 3 trillion gallons of unwanted water use each year in the U.S. alone, costing us $70 billion. With water, a little knowledge goes a long way. H2know helps you save money and improve our water use. Mark Kovscek, Founder & CEO Mark is an entrepreneur and mathematician with over 25 years of experience solving complex challenges with data science. He has led early stage analytic startups and global multi-disciplined teams. He earned his degree in Applied Mathematics and Industrial Management from Carnegie Mellon University. If not in the Lab, Mark may be found building something, doing musical theater, or getting lost in the woods. Jody Smith, Engineering Jody is a seasoned expert in systems architecture, full- stack development and DevOps. He has been on the founding team of companies that deliver SaaS products to the Fortune 500. He has built and managed platforms to provide scalable data management, machine learning, operations, and reporting. He wrote his first program on a Commodore SuperPET 9000. Jody is also an active and talented musician, songwriter, and composer. Rich Boniface, Engineering Rich has designed and built complex data services for over two decades for large and critical systems at companies such as Citi and ADP. He earned a Master of Science in Computer Science from Montclair State University, where he is also an Adjunct Professor. Rich can often be found somewhere in the middle of restoring a 1970’s vintage pinball machine or baking German pretzels from scratch. Brian Fox, Engineering Brian is a Solution Architect and Software Engineer with over 20 years of experience in both the Commercial and Government sectors. His work spans from web applications and big data processing to DevOps and site reliability engineering. He earned his degree in Mathematics from the University of Maryland. Outside of work, Brian enjoys cooking and improving his golf game. Aviv Roth, Engineering Aviv is a Senior Software Engineer and Systems Architect with over 2 decades of experience. He has specialized in backend and database technologies on multiple SaaS platforms in multiple industries. He is passionate about software quality, testing, and robust deployment processes. He earned a Music degree from Brown University. Outside of work, Aviv enjoys traveling and spending time with his wife and cats. Ken Higbee, Hardware Ken is an expert in IoT software and hardware development, including digital signal processing and cloud infrastructure. He has worked with several public and private companies to develop bleeding-edge products to help businesses to lead in their field. Ken has developed products that help people live more fulfilling lives. He wrote his first program on an Imsai 8080. Ken enjoys time with his family sailing, skiing, and adventuring. Julie Aylmer, Data Science Julie is an analytics leader with over 25 years developing data science solutions, building teams, and growing companies. She is an expert in predictive modeling and developing analytic and data-driven products. She earned a Masters degree in Mathematics from DePaul University. Julie grew up as a plumber’s daughter; Conservation Labs is the culmination of her childhood training and professional career. She’s a huge Cubs fan! Brian Brazon, Data Science Brian is a recent graduate of Carnegie Mellon University with a degree in Applied Mathematics and Operations Research. He is highly proficient in R and his research includes unsupervised classification techniques for time series data. If Brian isn’t coding in R, you can find him on the slopes or in the gym. Olivia Dehlin, Data Science Olivia is a recent graduate of West Virginia University with a degree in Industrial Engineering. She is applying quality control and optimization methods to improve data, machine learning approach, and reporting insights. Olivia can often be seen with binoculars nearby, she is an ornithologist and keeps a bird book. Nancy Haring, Data Science Nancy is a veteran data scientist with deep machine learning experience across a number of data types, analytic methods, and disciplines including risk, sales, and marketing sciences. She earned her MBA from the Keller Graduate School of Management and a few music degrees from Illinois State University. Nancy was an enthusiastic collector of fast food toys but now uses that energy for healthy cooking and health trends. Eric Winters, Data Science Eric has worked in the predictive analytics space over the past 20 years, supporting various industries such as retail, financial services, CPG and e-commerce. At Conservation Labs, Eric will focus on operationalizing processes and developing new solutions to support CL’s mission. He earned his MS in Statistics at The University of Akron. On the weekends, you may find Eric on the links o

Works wherever you write Gmail Google Docs Microsoft Word Notion Slack Any browser What is Penpal Writing intelligence that actually knows you. Most writing tools patch your mistakes. Penpal learns your patterns — your phrasing, vocabulary, sentence structures — and makes sure every word you write still sounds like you . It runs invisibly in the background across your entire screen, not locked inside a single app. No tab-switching. No copy-pasting. Just better writing, everywhere you already work. penpal — active // Passive mode running across workspace ✓ Voice profile loaded (487 samples) ✓ Grammar engine running ✓ Fact-check layer standby ── Monitoring: Gmail, Notion, Docs ⚡ Suggestion ready "sounds a bit formal for your usual tone" → rewrite in your voice? // Citations detected in draft → 3 sources auto-formatted [APA] ▋ Core Features Everything you need. Nothing you don't. 🎙️ Voice Profiling Builds a living model of your writing — vocabulary, phrasing, tone, rhythm — so every output sounds authentically like you, not a generic AI. ✍️ Real-Time Grammar & Clarity Catches errors and flags awkward phrasing passively in the background — no interruptions, no tab-switching, no friction to your flow. 🔍 Intelligent Fact-Checking The Logic Teacher engine assesses argument structure and verifies factual claims in real time, so your research actually holds up under scrutiny. 📚 Citation Discovery Automatically finds and formats citations for your claims — APA, MLA, Chicago — without you leaving the document or opening a separate tool. 🌐 Multi-Language Support Built for global writers. Penpal translates and adapts content across languages while preserving the voice and tone you've built — not flattening it. 🔒 No-Train Architecture Your writing never trains public models. Isolated processing ensures your unpublished work, research, and IP stay exclusively yours. How It Works Two modes. One seamless experience. Penpal works in the background by default and steps forward when you need it — no app-switching, no disruptive prompts. Passive Mode Always on. Never in the way. Runs silently while you write — learning, monitoring, and flagging without interrupting your flow. Real-time grammar and clarity monitoring Tone and voice consistency checks Continuous voice profile refinement Surfaces suggestions on your terms Active Mode Your co-author. On demand. When you want Penpal to step in, it rewrites, summarizes, expands, or restructures — always in your voice, not some generic AI's. Rewrite in your voice Summarise or expand sections Restructure for clarity and flow Auto-cite and fact-check on request Why Penpal Not another writing tool. A writing layer. The Huffman Librarian Memory that compounds over time. A self-organizing memory system using embeddings to dynamically prioritize your unique characteristics — tone, vocabulary, stylistic nuances. The more you use it, the better it knows you. That's a moat no competitor can copy. The Logic Teacher Arguments that actually hold up. Constructs dynamic logic pipelines to assess the integrity of your claims and reasoning — not just grammar, but whether your arguments are structurally sound. Critical for research, essays, and high-stakes professional writing. Cross-Platform Native Everywhere, not just somewhere. Unlike tools locked in a single app, Penpal operates at the screen level — simultaneously available in Gmail, Google Docs, Word, Notion, Slack, and any browser. One tool. Every surface you already use. Privacy First Your IP stays yours. Built on a strict no-train architecture. Your unpublished research, sensitive documents, and original writing are never used to fine-tune public models. Isolated processing, full stop. How We Compare Every tool does one thing. Penpal does all of it — and it actually learns who you are. items.text_snippet: Careers · Shopthru.ai Shopthru .ai Home Product Use Cases Team Blog Changelog Book a demo Demo Jump ⌘K ⌘K Jump 00 · Careers We’re hiring. Small team. Founding roles. Shopthru.ai is a small team, growing deliberately. Every hire is a founding hire and gets a vertical of the OS to own. The roles below are the ones we’re actively talking to people for. Founding Engineer Full-time · Pittsburgh / Remote Own a vertical of the OS end to end. Agent runtime, ledger, simulation, or the inbox. Comfortable with Python, TypeScript, and decisions that ship to production the same week. Founding Designer Full-time · Pittsburgh / Remote Design the surface of the agent. Inbox, approval console, simulation gate. The product is dense by nature; the craft is making density legible. Founding Sales / Partnerships Full-time · Remote First commercial hire. Run founder-led pipeline into mid-market DTC and platform partnerships across Shopify, Medusa, and the agentic checkout protocols. Founding ML / Research Full-time · Pittsburgh / Remote Push the brain of the system. Retrieval, evaluation, and the scoring layer that decides what an agent recommends. CMU LTI background welcome. 01 · What we look for Operators, not spectators. Taste, range, and a bias to ship. We hire for taste, range, and the willingness to write the first version yourself. The team is small enough that every decision is legible, and every commit is felt by the next customer demo. We don’t care where you went. We care what you’ve shipped, what you’ve broken, and what you’d rebuild if you started today. 02 · How to apply One email. No portal, no form. Send a note to hello@shopthru.ai with the role in the subject and a link to something you’ve made. We read every one. hello@shopthru.ai The next billion shoppers won’t be human. We’re building the rails. I’m a brand owner I’m an investor Brief our specialists. 12 agents waiting in the Inbox. Tell them what you’re shipping. A (still-human) co-founder will reply within one business day. Your name Work email Brand Brand URL — optional What’s on the brief? — optional Website Brief the agents or email hello@shopthru.ai We use what you send to reply, and nothing else. If AI is becoming the shopper, who’s looking out for the brands? That question is the company. 02 · Founders Two operators. One thesis. Co-founder · CEO Vishal Verma 10 yrs AI engineering · shipped to 150M+ users at Dream11 CMU CLeaR Group · ETH Zürich NeurIPS author & reviewer Co-founder · CTO Mantej Gill 7 US patents in applied ML · time series & anomaly detection 7 yrs AI Engineering @ Hewlett Packard Enterprise R&D · 2 prior startups CMU CLeaR Group researcher · NASA Space Apps winner We’ve spent a decade building the ML that now powers AI commerce. We know how these models reason, and how to make them reason about your brand . 03 · Origin Brands were invisible. So we built the layer that makes them legible. We’re engineers from Carnegie Mellon and researchers at CLeaR Lab. We spent months studying how ChatGPT, Perplexity and Gemini actually pick products, then built the causal-inference layer that gives brands SKU-level intelligence in those channels, not surface-level dashboards. Carnegie Mellon University Causal ML · CMU-CLeaR Group 04 · Thesis The Agentic OS for AI Commerce. Founded at Carnegie Mellon. Shopthru.ai is building the operating system commerce will run on once the buyer is an agent. Not a dashboard. Not a copilot. The substrate underneath. We started Shopthru.ai at Carnegie Mellon in 2025, between the language technologies labs and the Tepper studios. The premise was simple. The next billion shoppers wouldn’t be human, and the brands that won them wouldn’t be the ones with the best landing pages. They’d be the ones the agents trusted. Most of what calls itself AI in commerce today is an assistant that suggests. We’re building agents that act. Agents that audit your visibility across the LLMs that matter, fix the gaps in your context, prove the lift in simulation, and ship the change to production with a human in the loop. The whole loop, end to end, on rails. We’re shipping the OS, not the SaaS. A protocol layer for brands that intend to be picked, not just listed. 05 · Principles Four values. Non-negotiable. 01 Transparency You see exactly how AI assistants see your brand. No black boxes. 02 Agility AI commerce shifts daily. The platform adapts in the same beat. 03 Precision SKU-level insight, not surface-level guesses. Every product, every platform, every prompt. 04 Empowerment We augment marketing teams. We do not replace them. Get in touch Talk to the founders. Reply within 24 hours. No funnel, no SDR. hello@shopthru.ai LinkedIn

items.text_snippet: Frequently Asked Questions | Remit-Scout Skip to main content Remit-Scout Dashboard Compare Providers Guides Sign in Get Plus Home Frequently Asked Questions Frequently Asked Questions Answers about how Remit‑Scout works: how we collect quotes, how we rank providers, how to read results, and what you get with Remit‑Scout Plus. Remit‑Scout is a comparison and research product. We don't hold, move, or transmit money. When you choose a provider, you complete your transfer directly on the provider's licensed website or app. No pay-to-rank Timestamped quotes We don't move money Report a problem Quick Navigation Getting started Pricing, quotes, and accuracy Rankings and Remit‑Score Providers, safety, and availability Remit‑Scout Plus Partnerships and how we make money Privacy and data Reporting issues and support Getting started What is Remit‑Scout? Remit‑Scout is an independent comparison platform for international money transfers. We collect quotes, standardize fees and FX markup into comparable numbers, and highlight the metric most people care about: what the recipient should receive for the scenario you entered. You can compare providers side by side, then click through to the provider you choose to complete the transfer. Do you send money for me? No. Remit‑Scout does not process transfers and never touches your funds. We show you comparison results and then link you to the provider you choose. Your transfer happens on that provider's platform, under their identity verification and compliance rules. How do I compare providers on Remit‑Scout? Enter your send country, receive country, currency, amount, and (where available) payout method. We fetch quotes from multiple providers and standardize the results into comparable numbers, especially Recipient gets . When you choose a provider, you click through to complete the transfer on that provider’s checkout. Why do results change when I change the amount or payout method? Remittance pricing isn’t one flat price. A provider may be strong at $200 and less competitive at $2,000. Pricing can also change by payment method (bank vs card), payout method (bank deposit vs cash pickup), and speed options. A comparison only makes sense when it matches your real scenario, so Remit‑Scout recalculates results based on your inputs. Pricing, quotes, and accuracy What does "Recipient gets" mean? "Recipient gets" is our best estimate of what the recipient should receive after fees and FX markup for the specific scenario you entered. It’s practical because it answers the question most senders actually care about: what should arrive? Example: Send: $500 USD Provider A: $5 fee, 18.00 rate → 8,910 MXN Provider B: $1.99 fee, 18.45 rate → 9,188 MXN That’s 278 MXN more delivered on the same transfer, even if both advertise “low fees”. We calculate this as: \[\text{recipient gets} = (\text{send amount} - \text{fees}) \times \text{provider FX rate}\] What does "Total cost" include? Total cost includes everything that reduces what your recipient should receive: Stated transfer fee: the upfront charge you see FX markup: the difference between a provider’s rate and a reference mid-market rate at the same time ⚠️ The hidden markup problem Example: if the reference USD→MXN rate is 18.50 but a provider offers 18.00, that’s roughly a 2.7% markup . On a $500 transfer, that’s meaningful, even before any stated fee. Some providers advertise “$0 fees” but price through the exchange rate. Total cost helps you compare apples to apples. Why might the provider checkout show a different price than Remit‑Scout? Checkout can differ from a captured quote. Common reasons include: Payment method: bank vs card pricing can differ Promotions: offers that depend on user status, codes, or targeted eligibility KYC: verification steps can change eligibility, speed, or fees Local rules: corridor-specific requirements or payout constraints FX movement: rates can move between the time a quote is captured and the time you checkout 💡 Quick checklist Match payment method, payout method, and amount Check for promotions or codes Check the quote timestamp The provider checkout is always the final source of truth. If you see a mismatch that looks systematic, report it with corridor, amount, time, and a screenshot if possible. How often do you update rates? We refresh quotes regularly, especially on popular corridors. Update frequency varies by corridor, payment method, and data source. Every quote is timestamped so you can judge freshness. Where do you get your pricing data? We typically collect pricing via: Direct provider data feeds (most consistent when available) Partner data feeds (structured exports) Public quote capture from provider quote flows (coverage varies) We normalize that data into a standardized comparison. Read our methodology for details. Do you include promo codes and discounts? Sometimes. If a provider applies an automatic promotion in the quote flow we capture, you may see it reflected. Many promotions depend on account status, a code, or targeted eligibility, so they can’t always be captured universally. That’s why we emphasize Recipient gets as a best estimate and recommend verifying the final checkout amount. Rankings and Remit‑Score How are providers ranked? We rank providers by delivered outcome and total cost for the scenario you entered, then surface additional signals like payout method availability, speed, and reliability where available. The goal is simple: show the options that should deliver the best outcome, not the best marketing. What is Remit‑Score? Remit‑Score is a 0–10 score designed to summarize overall value and usability in one number. It’s built from measurable signals, weighted by importance: Delivered Value (40%): fees + FX markup and delivered outcome for the scenario shown Reliability & Success (20%): quote success rate and data freshness signals Friction & Speed (15%): ETA and speed buckets where available Support & Refunds (15%): policy and support signals where available Trust & Safety (10%): licensing and safety signals where available Scores like 9.5 , 8.4 , or 7.2 are shorthand, not pay-to-play. See our full methodology for details. Can providers pay to rank higher? No. Providers cannot pay to appear higher, improve a Remit‑Score, or change how we sort results. If a provider offers better delivered value for your corridor and amount, they should rank better, whether or not we have a commercial relationship. Do affiliate relationships affect rankings or Remit‑Score? No. If we earn a commission for a referral, we disclose it clearly. But commissions do not change scoring, ranking, or sorting. The comparison is driven by data. Learn more about partnerships . Why would a provider with a higher fee still appear high? Sometimes a provider with a higher visible fee still delivers strong value due to a better exchange rate, faster delivery option, higher reliability, or better customer support outcomes. The "best" option depends on what you prioritize: cost, speed, payout method, or trust factors. Providers, safety, and availability Do you only list licensed or regulated providers? We aim to cover established providers and to label coverage and availability transparently. Regulation varies by country, corridor, and product type, so the “right” license can differ across markets. Where public licensing information or registry entries are available, we use them as part of our trust and labeling approach. Why don't I see the same providers for every corridor? Not every provider supports every send/receive pair, payout method, or amount. Some providers may support bank deposit but not cash pickup in a specific country, or may not operate in a particular U.S. state or region. Is Remit‑Scout responsible if something goes wrong with my transfer? No. The provider you choose is responsible for processing your transfer and handling disputes. items.text_snippet: About Remit-Scout | Independent Money Transfer Comparisons Skip to main content Remit-Scout Dashboard Compare Providers Guides Sign in Get Plus 🇺🇸 Compare Rates 🇺🇸 Compare Rates Home About Us About Remit-Scout The true cost of sending money is hidden in the spread. We make it visible . Remit-Scout is an independent comparison platform that shows you what your recipient will actually receive . After every fee, markup, and spread is accounted for. Independent. Algorithmic. Built for clarity. Incubated at the Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship, Carnegie Mellon University . The problem Most people sending money abroad compare the advertised fee. That's the wrong number. Providers bury their real margin in the exchange rate, a markup on the mid-market rate that's invisible until after you've committed. A provider charging $0 in fees can still cost 3–5% more than a competitor charging $8. The difference lives entirely in the spread. Without normalizing fees and FX markup together, any comparison is incomplete. We built one number, Net Delivered Value , that captures the full cost so you can compare on outcome, not marketing copy. Algorithmic Neutrality Rankings are determined purely by mathematical outcome. Marketing budgets cannot buy position; our sort order is immutable. Net-Value Indexing We ignore headline rates. Our engine calculates the final settlement amount, factoring in upfront fees and the hidden FX spread markup. Open Data Protocol Trust requires verification. We maintain an open channel for data correction. If a provider updates their pricing logic, our system adapts within 24 hours. How it works We monitor eligible providers and corridors where recent, rights-cleared observations exist. Approved quote evidence is normalized against independent FX benchmarks, and suppressed rows stay visible when source rights, freshness, or methodology gates do not pass. TEER True Effective Exchange Rate The net rate your recipient receives after all fees and FX markup are deducted. The only number that tells you what actually arrives. RCI Cost Friction RCI Quote-derived transfer-cost friction expressed against a benchmark. It stays separate from beta/non-price constraint signals. RVI Remittance Volatility Index How much pricing varies across providers in a corridor. High volatility signals that significant savings are available for those who compare. How a comparison works Collect quotes Observed quotes are gathered from approved provider sources where available for the selected corridor and payment method. Normalize total cost Fees and FX markup are combined into a single figure: what the recipient should receive . Rank by outcome Results are ranked by delivered value, not advertising spend. The explanation shows what's driving the difference. Read the full methodology How we collect quotes, compute indices, and verify provider coverage. A note on quotes Rates can change between quote and checkout due to promotional offers, KYC requirements, payment method selection, and provider rules. Always confirm the final amount on the provider's checkout screen before completing your transfer. Omar Ghabayen Founder, Remit-Scout Carnegie Mellon University LinkedIn Origin "When I first moved to the US for Carnegie Mellon, my family in Jordan would send money to help me settle in. Every time, $20-30 vanished, split between the sending and receiving banks. Nobody could explain where it went. I started digging and discovered the real cost was buried in the FX spread, not the advertised fee. The comparison sites everyone trusted were only looking at half the picture. That gap, between what people think they're paying and what they actually pay, is why Remit-Scout exists. We answer one question: how much will actually arrive?" "Global finance is complex. The decision shouldn't be." Reviewed: February 19, 2026 Our standards We built Remit-Scout for people who want a straight answer. These are the commitments we don't negotiate on. Outcome-first ranking We rank by what the recipient receives, not a headline rate or fee. The best provider is the one that delivers the most. No pay-to-rank Providers cannot buy placement in our organic results. Rankings are computed algorithmically and cannot be influenced by commercial relationships. Editorial independence If we earn affiliate commissions, they are fully disclosed and strictly firewalled from the ranking algorithm. Your trust is more valuable than any partnership. Quotes are refreshed throughout the day across monitored corridors, benchmarked against independent FX rate sources, and verified through periodic spot-check transfers on selected routes. Freshness varies by provider and route, and discrepancies reported by users are investigated and corrected. Transparency We publish everything that matters: how we collect data, how we rank providers, and how we earn revenue. Our methodology How we collect quotes, compute indices, and verify coverage. How we make money Affiliate disclosure and how we stay independent. Partnerships What partnerships mean and what they do not. FAQs Quick answers about accuracy, rankings, and updates. Frequently asked questions How does Remit-Scout make money? We may earn an affiliate commission when you click a provider link and complete a transfer. These partnerships never influence rankings: providers cannot pay to rank higher. Read our revenue disclosure . Do you hold or move my money? No. Remit-Scout is a comparison tool. The transfer happens directly between you and the licensed provider you choose. We never touch your funds. What does "recipient gets" mean? The amount your recipient should receive after all fees and FX markup are applied. It reflects the real-world outcome, not a headline rate. How do you verify provider data? We combine provider APIs, partner feeds, and periodic spot-check transfers on selected corridors. Discrepancies reported by users are investigated and corrected within 24 hours. How often are rates updated? High-volume corridors refresh continuously; long-tail corridors refresh less frequently. items.text_snippet: Building your AI future one Agent at a time Products About us Contact Build your First Agent 2026-01-15 10 min read Announcing Paladio AI’s AEC Agent – the Agentic AI to Automate Construction Document Understanding Why Construction Document Understanding Matters The Architecture, Engineering, and Construction (AEC) industry runs on documents. Drawings, schedules, specifications, and revisions define scope, cost, and risk across the entire project lifecycle. Yet these documents were never designed for machines. A single construction drawing set can exceed 100 pages and combine vector floor plans, dense schedules, scanned text, symbols, legends, and cross-referenced specifications. Meaning is distributed across pages and formats, not contained in linear text. Unlocking this information reliably enables critical downstream workflows: Quantity takeoffs for estimating and procurement Value engineering (VE) to evaluate cost and scope alternatives Conversational analysis to query drawings and specifications directly Despite recent advances in large language models (LLMs), production-scale construction document understanding remains unsolved. Understanding construction documents at scale is not a model problem alone — it is a systems problem. General Approach The Paladio AEC Agent approaches construction document understanding as a coordinated, agentic workflow rather than a single extraction task. Instead of treating a drawing set as unstructured text or images, the system decomposes documents into semantically meaningful units, reasons about the role each unit plays within the overall set, and applies specialized processing paths accordingly. Multiple agents collaborate to interpret content, validate signals, and reconcile information across pages, allowing the system to construct a consistent, document-level representation from heterogeneous inputs. This design enables robust handling of large, variable drawing sets while maintaining predictable behavior across accuracy, latency, and cost constraints. Evaluation Scope & Methodology Evaluating an agentic system for construction document understanding requires balancing accuracy, latency, and cost across different stages of the construction lifecycle. The acceptable trade-offs between these factors vary by use case. During early design and conceptual evaluation, teams often seek directional insight into how design changes affect scope and cost, where single-digit precision in quantities may not be critical. In contrast, during detailed estimating and construction execution, even small errors in product specifications or quantities can propagate into procurement mistakes and downstream risk. To build confidence that the Paladio AEC Agent can operate reliably across these scenarios, we evaluate performance along three dimensions: extraction quality , end-to-end execution characteristics , and operational predictability . Rather than optimizing for a single metric in isolation, the evaluation focuses on whether the system maintains stable, bounded behavior under real production constraints, including large document sizes, heterogeneous content, and repeated re-runs after revisions. The Real Constraints: Accuracy, Latency, and Cost In production AEC workflows, success is defined by three non-negotiable factors: Accuracy Missed quantities or misclassified schedules propagate downstream into pricing, procurement, and bid risk. Latency Processing must align with estimating and procurement timelines, including re-runs after drawing revisions. Cost predictability Per-document inference costs must remain bounded across large project volumes. Many off-the-shelf LLM pipelines are optimized for flexibility or small-scale tasks, but can exhibit trade-offs when all three constraints are applied simultaneously. We also compare to some popular off-the-shelf LLMs that do the job fully automatically by simply taking the contents of each LLM page, and extract contents directly or do the take-off directly. The observations described below reflect internal evaluations conducted on representative construction drawing sets under specific production constraints (page count, document variability, and takeoff completeness requirements). Results may vary depending on document characteristics, system configurations, prompts, tooling, and model versions. This analysis is not intended as a universal benchmark. Early Takeaway: Task-Level Performance on a 100-Page Drawing Set Before diving into detailed metrics, one result consistently surfaced during evaluations: System Takeoff Accuracy End-to-End Latency Generic OCR + LLM pipeline ~0.72–0.75 Highly variable AEC Agent ~0.92 ~60 minutes (full pipeline) While generic pipelines may appear faster on isolated subtasks, end-to-end consistency and reconciliation proved to be the primary determinants of production reliability. For a deeper breakdown across extraction categories, see the measured performance table below. Benchmarking the Landscape: What We Evaluated Before developing our AEC Agent, we evaluated multiple model categories and pipeline designs across real construction drawing sets. Model Categories Evaluated Vision-based segmentation models (e.g., SAM) Layout-aware parsers (e.g., LayoutParser, Docling) General-purpose LLMs accessed via OCR + LLM pipelines Hybrid OCR + LLM systems Domain-tuned internal models Test Characteristics 50–150 page drawing sets Mixed plan-heavy and schedule-heavy documents High-density tabular schedules Real-world noise (inconsistent formatting, abbreviations, missing legends) All evaluations were conducted using publicly available models and standard tooling configurations available at the time of testing. Are Vision-Only and Layout-Only Approaches Enough? Short answer: they help, but they are not sufficient for production-grade AEC takeoffs. Key Findings Vision-only models reliably identify where content exists, but struggle to determine what that content represents. Layout-aware parsers improve text and table extraction, yet break down when document structure varies or cross-page reasoning is required. Both approaches add preprocessing value, but fall short as end-to-end solutions for construction takeoffs at scale. What We Observed in Practice Vision-based segmentation models Accurately isolate regions such as tables, drawings, and annotations. Lack semantic understanding to differentiate schedules from notes or legends. Require extensive downstream logic to convert detected regions into construction-ready quantities. Layout-aware parsers Improve separation of text blocks and tables compared to raw OCR. Become brittle when layouts shift slightly between pages. Do not capture drawing semantics or reconcile information across pages. In isolation, these approaches perform well on individual pages. In production drawing sets, however, their limitations compound as page count and variability increase. How Far Do Generic OCR + LLM Pipelines Actually Go? High-level takeaway: generic OCR + LLM pipelines perform well on small subsets, but struggle to maintain consistency, predictability, and cost control at full document scale. Key Findings Strong semantic reasoning on isolated pages. Degrading performance as document size and heterogeneity increase. Rising latency and highly variable costs under production workloads. What Happens at Scale As drawing sets grow larger and more complex, we consistently observed: Context fragmentation caused by text-based chunking. Inconsistent outputs across pages processed independently. Table truncation driven by token limits. Increased latency from parallel LLM calls. Cost variability that scaled with retries and document size. Most importantly, schedules, plans, and notes were typically processed using identical logic, leading to ambiguity during extraction and aggregation. items.text_snippet: Civys · Pre-compliance intelligence Skip to content CV Civys . Pre-compliance intelligence Know what's required. Know what's unclear. Civys turns legal and policy text into an audit-ready Brief: every obligation classified, every claim traced to its section, and every gap the text leaves open stated plainly. It is built to say “no conclusion available” : not to guess. Reading California CCPA OBL-001 Mandatory High DIRECT, §1798.100(b) Disclosure at collection. A business must inform consumers, at or before the point of collection, of the categories of personal information collected and the purposes for use. OBL-005 Conditional High DIRECT, §1798.120(a) Opt-out of sale. If a consumer directs a business that sells personal information not to sell it, the business must comply. NC-001 No conclusion available How quickly must a business respond to a deletion request? Reason: the text is silent. It sets no response deadline, so Civys declines to infer one. Four kinds of certainty. A Brief is a structured record, not a chat reply. It separates what the text requires from what it merely permits, who it touches, and, deliberately, what it never resolves. 01 / CLASSIFICATION Obligation classification Every requirement sorted as mandatory, discretionary, or conditional, driven by the text's own signal words, with a confidence level on each. Mandatory Discretionary Conditional 02 / TRACEABILITY Source traceability Each claim carries a tag and section citation, so a reviewer can check it against the original text in seconds, not paragraphs. DIRECT PARAPHRASE INFERENCE INTERPRETATION 03 / APPLICABILITY Scope & applicability A clear map of who is covered, who is explicitly excluded, and which areas the text leaves silent, each cited to its source. Covered Excluded Silent 04 / UNCERTAINTY Uncertainty register Undefined terms, flexible language, and questions the text cannot answer, listed, not hidden. The section that prevents false confidence. UNDEFINED_TERM NO CONCLUSION AVAILABLE The method Defined as much by what it refuses to do. Most tools optimize for a fluent answer. Civys optimizes for a defensible one, which sometimes means declining to answer at all. not a summarizer Summaries smooth over ambiguity. A Brief discloses it, flagging every place the text is unclear instead of papering over it. not a chatbot Chat implies fluency over correctness. A Brief is an immutable record with an ID, a status, and an audit trail, a system of record, not a conversation. not legal advice Civys interprets the specific text in front of it and cites its work. items.title: About · Civys
items.text_snippet: About · Civys Skip to content CV Civys . Generate Browse Briefs Compare Settings About Sign in Sign out About Civys Policy analysis that says “I don’t know.” Civys turns policy text into structured briefs. It tells you what’s required, what’s optional, and—importantly—what the text doesn’t answer. 01 What it does Three things, clearly. Obligations Sorts requirements into mandatory (“must”), discretionary (“may”), and conditional (“if/when”). Each one cites the exact section. Scope Shows who’s covered, who’s excluded, and what the policy is silent about. No assumptions. Gaps Flags undefined terms, vague language, and missing details. Points out what needs clarification. 02 How it works Four steps. Paste your policy text. Copy from a PDF, website, or document. Works with bills, regulations, contracts, internal policies. Set your context. Tell us your jurisdiction and role. This scopes the analysis to what matters to you. Get your brief. In about 30 seconds, you’ll have a structured breakdown of obligations, scope, and gaps. Export or save. Download as PDF for your files, or save to your account to reference later. 03 What’s in a Brief The actual output. Brief overview A 2–3 sentence summary of what the policy does and who it affects. No fluff. Obligations section Every requirement tagged as MANDATORY, DISCRETIONARY, or CONDITIONAL with the source section cited. Scope section Who’s covered (COVERED), who’s exempt (EXCLUDED), and what’s not mentioned (SILENT). Uncertainty section Undefined terms, flexible language, and implementation gaps that need human judgment. 04 How it’s different Not a chatbot. Shows its sources. Every claim links back to the original text with section numbers. You can verify everything. Admits uncertainty. When the text is unclear or silent, it says so. No confident-sounding guesses. Structured output. Same format every time. Easy to compare across policies and share with your team. No hallucinations. If it’s not in the text, it won’t appear in the brief. Period. Designed for professionals. Built for people who face consequences if they get the interpretation wrong. 05 Who it’s for People who need to get it right. Government staff Figure out what new state or federal regulations actually require your department to do. Compliance teams Document your interpretation with sources before an auditor asks “how did you determine that?” Legal teams Get a first pass on policy obligations without spending hours reading dense legislative text. 06 Example use cases What people use it for. New regulation drops. A federal agency releases new rules. You need to know what applies to your organization by Friday. Grant compliance. You’re administering a grant and need to document which requirements are mandatory vs. recommended. Policy comparison. The state updated a law. You need to see what changed from the previous version. Audit prep. Auditors are coming. You need documentation showing how you interpreted the compliance requirements. Contract review. A vendor contract has compliance language. You need to know what you’re actually agreeing to. 07 What it doesn’t do Setting expectations. Not legal advice. Civys helps you understand text, but it doesn’t replace a lawyer for important decisions. Won’t make judgment calls. If the text is ambiguous, we flag it. We don’t pick an interpretation for you. Can’t read your mind. We analyze the text you give us. We don’t know your organization’s specific situation. Not a search engine. We analyze text you provide. We don’t search for policies or pull them from databases (except Congress.gov bills). Try it. Paste any policy text and get a structured brief in about 30 seconds. Parameters query Search term (e.g., "climate", "healthcare reform") congress Congress number (default: 118). Range: 93-118 type Bill type: hr , s , hjres , sjres , hconres , sconres limit Results per page (default: 20, max: 100) offset Pagination offset sort Sort order: updateDate+desc , updateDate+asc Example Response { "bills": [ { "congress": 118, "type": "HR", "number": "4821", "title": "Clean Energy Innovation Act", "introducedDate": "2024-01-15", "latestAction": "Referred to committee" } ], "pagination": { "count": 50, "next": "..." } } GET /api/bills/{billId} Get detailed bill information Returns full text, actions history, cosponsors, and committee referrals. Parameters billId Format: congress-type-number (e.g., 118-hr-1234 ) Example Response { "billId": "118-hr-1234", "title": "Example Act of 2024", "shortTitle": "Example Act", "introducedDate": "2024-01-15", "sponsor": { "name": "Rep. Smith, John", "party": "D", "state": "CA" }, "cosponsors": { "count": 45, "list": [...] }, "committees": [...], "actions": [...], "summary": { "text": "..." }, "latestTextUrl": "https://..." } GET /api/analyze Structured policy interpretation Choose from five analysis types to get the insights you need. Parameters bill Required. Bill ID (e.g., 118-hr-1234 ) type Analysis type (default: summary ) Analysis Types summary Concise 2-3 paragraph overview of the bill's purpose, key provisions, and who it affects. impact Detailed impact analysis covering affected groups, economic implications, social implications, and implementation challenges. pros-cons Balanced list of 3-5 arguments for and against the bill with explanations. timeline Likely legislative timeline and next steps based on current status and historical patterns. structured Structured interpretation with obligation classification and section citations. Example Request curl "https://civys.vercel.app/api/analyze?bill=118-hr-1&type=pros-cons" \ -H "X-API-Key: pl_live_your_key" Example Response { "success": true, "bill": { "id": "118-hr-1", "title": "Lower Energy Costs Act", "number": "HR 1", "congress": "118" }, "analysis": { "type": "pros-cons", "typeName": "Pros and Cons", "content": "## Pros\n1. **Reduces energy costs**..." } } POST /api/analyze Custom AI analysis with your prompts Full control over system instructions and user queries. Request Body system Required. System prompt defining the AI's role and behavior user Required. User prompt with the content to analyze max_tokens Maximum response length (default: 4096) Example Request curl -X POST "https://civys.vercel.app/api/analyze" \ -H "X-API-Key: pl_live_your_key" \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{ "system": "You are a tax policy expert.", "user": "Explain how HR 1234 affects small businesses.", "max_tokens": 2048 }' 04 Authentication How to authenticate your API requests API Key (Recommended) Include your API key in the X-API-Key header: curl "https://civys.vercel.app/api/bills" \ -H "X-API-Key: pl_live_your_key_here" Bearer Token For Firebase-authenticated users, use the Authorization header: curl "https://civys.vercel.app/api/bills" \ -H "Authorization: Bearer your_firebase_token" Error Responses 401 Authentication required - missing or invalid API key 400 Bad request - missing required parameters 404 Not found - bill or member doesn't exist 429 Rate limit exceeded - slow down requests 500 Server error - try again later 05 Rate Limits & Pricing Choose the plan that fits your needs Free $0 /month 10 requests/minute 100 requests/day Bills & search endpoints Community support Current Plan Popular Pro $49 /month 100 requests/minute 5,000 requests/day All endpoints + predictions Voting patterns data Priority support Coming Soon Enterprise Custom Unlimited requests Custom rate limits Dedicated support SLA guarantees Contact Us Civys Pre-compliance intelligence. This is me painting it 5 years ago before our first guest arrived ⬇️ Week after week, small things would go wrong. Remotes missing. Scuffs on walls. A broken drawer handle we didn't catch until the guest complained about it in a review The problem wasn't bad guests or bad cleaners. The problem was we had no system to track what changed between stays. As a computer vision engineer, I kept thinking... this should be solvable. If we can identify obstacles in real-time for self-driving vehicles, why can't we detect a missing remote or piece of furniture? 🤔 That's why I started RapidEye with Samuel Parks We're building AI that compares your property across turnovers and flags what changed. items.text_snippet: At Corporate Startup Lab ROAI Conference at the Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship at CMU - My Framer Site Home About Services Blog Contact Home About Services Blog Contact Apr 8, 2022 At Corporate Startup Lab ROAI Conference at the Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship at CMU At Corporate Startup Lab ROAI Conference at the Swartz Center for Entrepreneurship at CMU Understanding Strategic Planning At its essence, strategic planning encapsulates the art and science of charting a course for an organization, encompassing its aspirations, goals, and the means to achieve them. It's a forward-looking endeavor that requires a deep understanding of the organization's internal dynamics and external landscape. Through strategic planning, organizations articulate their vision, define their mission, and lay out a comprehensive strategy to navigate the complexities of the business environment. The Benefits Unveiled Strategic planning brings forth a plethora of benefits that extend beyond the boardroom and permeate throughout the organization's fabric. One of its most profound impacts lies in providing clarity and focus. By crystallizing the organization's purpose and direction, strategic planning ensures that every individual within the organization is aligned towards a common goal, thereby enhancing efficiency and productivity. Moreover, strategic planning fosters adaptability and resilience in the face of uncertainties. In today's volatile business environment, where change is the only constant, organizations equipped with a robust strategic plan possess the agility to respond to disruptions, mitigate risks, and capitalize on emerging opportunities. It serves as a shield against the unpredictable forces of the market, enabling organizations to steer through turbulent waters with confidence. Key Components of Strategic Planning A comprehensive strategic plan comprises various elements that work synergistically to propel the organization forward. It begins with a thorough assessment of the organization's internal capabilities and external environment. This involves conducting a SWOT (Strengths, Weaknesses, Opportunities, Threats) analysis to identify areas of competitive advantage and areas that require improvement. From there, organizations proceed to define their strategic objectives – the milestones they aim to achieve in pursuit of their vision. These objectives are not merely lofty aspirations but are grounded in realism, supported by actionable initiatives and measurable targets. A well-crafted strategic plan delineates the roadmap for achieving these objectives, outlining the necessary steps, timelines, and resource allocations. Embracing Strategic Planning for Success In conclusion, the power of strategic planning lies in its ability to transform visions into realities. It serves as a guiding light, illuminating the path towards organizational success amidst the complexities of the business landscape. By providing clarity of purpose, fostering adaptability, and aligning efforts, strategic planning empowers organizations to overcome challenges, capitalize on opportunities, and thrive in an ever-evolving marketplace. Embrace strategic planning as the cornerstone of your organization's journey towards enduring success. Ready to ship your pilot? Get started Mission control for everything you're building. Scaling encompasses various aspects of the business, including operations, sales and marketing, human resources, and technology. It involves optimizing processes, leveraging resources effectively, and capitalizing on economies of scale to drive growth and profitability. Identifying Growth Opportunities The first step in scaling your business is identifying growth opportunities that align with your vision and objectives. This involves conducting market research, analyzing industry trends, and understanding customer needs and preferences. By identifying untapped markets, emerging trends, and areas of competitive advantage, you can position your business for strategic growth and expansion. Developing a Scalable Business Model A scalable business model is essential for sustainable growth and expansion. This involves designing processes, systems, and structures that can accommodate growth without sacrificing efficiency or quality. It requires streamlining operations, automating repetitive tasks, and implementing scalable technologies to support increased demand and capacity. Investing in Infrastructure and Resources Scaling your business requires investment in infrastructure, resources, and talent to support increased demand and expansion. This may involve hiring additional staff, upgrading technology systems, or expanding physical facilities to accommodate growth. By investing strategically in infrastructure and resources, you can ensure that your business has the capacity and capabilities to scale effectively. Fostering Innovation and Adaptability Innovation is key to sustained growth and competitiveness in today's rapidly evolving business environment. As you scale your business, it's important to foster a culture of innovation and adaptability, encouraging experimentation, creativity, and continuous improvement. This may involve developing new products or services, entering new markets, or adopting new technologies to stay ahead of the curve. Building Strategic Partnerships Strategic partnerships can be instrumental in scaling your business by providing access to new markets, customers, and resources. Whether it's forming alliances with complementary businesses, partnering with suppliers or distributors, or collaborating with industry associations, strategic partnerships can help you accelerate growth and expand your reach more quickly and cost-effectively. items.title: CollAI — Autonomous SRE Agent
items.text_snippet: CollAI — Autonomous SRE Agent CollAI Demo How it works Why us Dashboard Enterprise-Grade Zero-Trust Architecture Zero-Trust AI Incident Response for FinTech. CollAI strips secrets and PII inside your VPC before AI ever sees the payload—three independent checks, one tight boundary. Fast for on-call, calm for compliance. If a scrub is wrong, flag it in chat: it is recorded for audit, and the next alert can be tighter without raw logs leaving your network. SOC 2 Type II-ready architecture · PCI-DSS-aligned controls · DORA-oriented operations · Docker edge agent · TLS-only cloud egress · Chat flags for bad scrubs Download Android app Open web dashboard Android available now. iOS coming soon. SOC 2 Type II Ready PCI-DSS Compliant Architecture Sanitize Before Cloud Egress CollAI Mobile Live Push alert Tap to open the incident room 1 /3 🚨 CRITICAL: production-api CPU 95% · error rate spiking · tap to open incident room Deep link → /chat/incident 2-minute product demo See CollAI move from alert to approved remediation. Watch a real incident flow: alert intake, AI diagnosis, human approval from mobile, resolution summary, and audit evidence from the same workflow. Open on YouTube Try dashboard connect — webhook — dashboard.trycollai.com 3 layers Independent edge scanners VPC Sanitize before egress < 30s To first diagnostic 1 URL Webhook to connect Resolve faster AI investigates the moment alerts fire. Root cause in seconds, not minutes. Less alert fatigue Context and suggested fixes before you're fully awake. Page only when it matters. Bad scrub? Flag it. Wrong redaction gets logged for security. New rules can land on your in-VPC agent so the next alert is cleaner—without shipping raw logs out to train models in our cloud. Works with your existing stack After install, update your webhook target to http://<agent-host-ip>:8080/intercept-alert Datadog PagerDuty Splunk CloudWatch Prometheus Alertmanager Azure OpenAI Kubernetes Terraform GitHub Datadog PagerDuty Splunk CloudWatch Prometheus Alertmanager Azure OpenAI Kubernetes Terraform GitHub How it works From alert to resolution in four steps. No runbooks. No context-switching. No waking up the whole team. No SDK migrations · Datadog · PagerDuty · Splunk · Alertmanager Step 01 Alert fires PagerDuty, Datadog, CloudWatch, or any webhook POSTs to the CollAI local agent running in your VPC. Step 02 Three-layer sanitization Regex strips known patterns. Entropy analysis catches obfuscated secrets. Contextual ML catches names, orgs, and structured PII that pattern lists alone often miss. Step 03 Proposed fix The AI proposes a specific action — restart instance, revert commit, scale pods — with a clear risk assessment. Step 04 You approve (or don't) Tap approve on your phone or type it in chat. Nothing runs without your explicit approval. What your team configures 1. Generate API key Create a CollAI API key in dashboard settings for the agent to authenticate cloud ingestion. 2. Run the VPC agent Install with Docker or the installer script. The agent listens on :8080 . 3. Point webhooks inward Send Datadog, PagerDuty, Splunk, or Alertmanager events to /intercept-alert ; the agent forwards sanitized JSON to CollAI. Zero‑Trust proof You control the boundary. Most “AI incident tools” ask you to paste logs into a prompt. That’s not acceptable in regulated environments. CollAI inserts a deterministic sanitization boundary inside your VPC, then forwards only scrubbed JSON to the cloud. Layer 1: Regex detects cards, SSNs, emails, IPs, API keys, and AWS access keys Layer 2: Entropy analysis catches high-entropy secrets that evade static patterns Layer 3: Local ML identifies names, orgs, and context-dependent PII — air-gapped, no external calls Every redaction is SHA-256 hashed and chained for tamper-evident audit compliance Data flow VPC → HTTPS → CollAI Cloud Before (inside your VPC) { "alert": "AKIA...", "email": "name@corp.com", "ip": "10.0.1.12" } After (sent to cloud) { "alert": "<REDACTED_AWS_KEY_a8f5c2>", "email": "<REDACTED_EMAIL_3b9e71>", "ip": "<REDACTED_IPV4_c4f0d8>" } Three detection layers · SHA-256 hashed placeholders · hash-chained audit trail · zero plaintext in transit. RAG in production today Retrieval is conditioned on verified sanitization. CollAI does not run "open" retrieval across raw logs. We only retrieve from sanitized incident knowledge, and only when the request proves it came through the edge sanitization boundary. Gate on verified edge path RAG retrieval is enabled only when local-agent sanitizer headers prove the payload came through the in-VPC scrubber path. Use sanitized corpus only CollAI stores and indexes sanitized incident summaries and reports, not raw telemetry. Retrieval context is assembled from that sanitized store. Keep retrieval incident-scoped Queries prioritize same-service and same-failure-pattern context so diagnostics are grounded in relevant prior incidents. Attach evidence to diagnosis Returned context is used to strengthen root-cause and remediation suggestions and is logged alongside the incident for auditability. Built for teams that can't afford downtime. AI that investigates the moment alerts fire. Real-time state, real root cause, real suggested fixes — you stay in control. Zero-Trust Sanitization Boundary Three independent detection layers — deterministic regex, Shannon entropy analysis, and contextual ML — scrub payloads inside your VPC before any data leaves your network. 1-Tap Approval Workflows Get root-cause analysis and proposed remediation scripts pushed to your phone. Destructive actions stay gated by an authenticated, explicit human approval and are logged for audit and rollback. Triager feedback → stronger edge rules False negative or false positive? Flag it where you already triage—dashboard or CollAI Mobile. Feedback lands in an auditable store for security owners, and when your agent accepts it, new patterns can wire straight into the running redaction engine (regex or contextual recognizers). That is operator-shaped adaptation at the boundary—not uploading telemetry to retrain a shared cloud model. Enterprise-Grade Compliance Built for SOC 2 Type II, PCI-DSS, and HIPAA architectures. Every decision is logged, secrets are redacted at the edge, and redaction evidence is hash-chained for review. IaC Native Deployment Docker-based edge agent, Terraform-friendly install, and declarative YAML policy packs. Point webhooks at `:8080` inside your VPC; outbound is TLS-only to CollAI cloud with your API key. Tamper-Evident Audit Trail Each redaction produces a SHA-256 fingerprint hash-chained to the previous event. Auditors can cryptographically verify no record was altered or removed after the fact. Purpose-Built Native Mobile CollAI is not a thin web wrapper. The mobile app is a dedicated incident workspace for triage, approvals, and follow-up actions on the move. Stop debugging in chat apps. Most incident tools are glorified pagers that force you to debug inside Slack. But chat apps weren't built for 2 AM server logs, multi-file code reviews, or architecture diagrams. It's a formatting nightmare. CollAI is a purpose-built mobile workspace. We built a standalone, native mobile environment specifically for engineering fires. Native log viewer & full terminal context Multimodal AI for diagrams and code — no laptop required CollAI vs. the 3 AM phone call. Traditional on-call costs you sleep, context, and time. CollAI handles the first 90% autonomously. items.text_snippet:
Reviva (https://joinreviva.com/) is the AI-native operating system for cash-pay healthcare and wellness — the first true system of action for a $100B+ market that has never had a dominant platform. Cash-pay practices (med spas, acupuncture clinics, integrative medicine, chiropractic) have been forced to stitch together 3–7 disconnected tools built for salons or insurance-based medicine. The software has always been too clunky for a non-technical demographic, too human-intensive to scale, and too fragmented to produce a winner. No company has ever taken a majority of this market — despite it being massive and growing fast.That changes now. Agentic AI means software can speak human for the first time — executing work on behalf of non-technical users, eliminating the switching costs that kept practices locked into bad software for years, and enabling a product-led growth motion that has never existed in this space.Valerie (Stanford, ex-NEA, ex-Assembled) and Jane (CMU, ex-Zoom, ex-AWS, 2× YC) built the system of record first — the HIPAA-compliant EHR, scheduling, payments, and clinical data layer that makes a true practice intelligence agent possible.
Industries: Enterprise Software/SaaS, Healthcare & BioTech
